ai.description: This caecilian reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark violet-brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a yellow-spotted venter. It is identified by its 280–300 primary annuli and lack of a sub-tentacular groove.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis kodaguensis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis kodaguensis* inhabits moist, evergreen tropical forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kodagu striped ichthyophis is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis kodaguensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females guarding the eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis kodaguensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, specifically found in the Kodagu district at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis kodaguensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted by individuals residing in moist, subterranean soil burrows.
